A0225.title: Physical-World Prompt Injection Detection
A0225.definition: Detection of visual, voice, and covert-audio prompt-injection attacks against embodied-intelligence VLA models in physical environments through instruction-source verification, multimodal injection-carrier recognition, and action-intent auditing.
A0225.description:
Physical-world prompt injection detection targets attacks that use environmental text, QR codes, printed patterns, projections, screen content, speaker audio, cloned speech, ultrasound, or covert-audio payloads to make a VLA model misinterpret instructions. It establishes detection capabilities across three dimensions. First, instruction-source and environmental-consistency verification binds operator speech, control terminals, and predefined tasks to trusted identities and channels; collects source, time, location, and task context; and downgrades, isolates, or rejects semantic instructions that cannot be attributed or conflict across channels. Second, multimodal injection-carrier recognition detects suddenly appearing high-contrast text, QR codes, unnatural patterns, and task-irrelevant signs in the visual channel, while analyzing speech transcripts, source location, speaker characteristics, ultrasonic-band energy, and covert-audio anomalies in the audio channel, using rules, thresholds, or models to classify suspicious payloads. Third, action-intent auditing validates whether the VLA output action sequence aligns with the current task context and safety boundaries before execution, triggering secondary confirmation for intent deviations.

This measure detects physical payloads that a model can interpret as instructions or semantic content. Signals that only cause sensor distortion, noise, or erroneous measurements should instead be handled by perception defenses such as sensor-anomaly detection and multisensor consistency checks. This measure combines environmental perception, trusted instruction sources, and action-layer validation as defense in depth, and complements A0178 (AIoT model security protection) and A0014 (tamper-proof mechanisms).
A0225.limitation: It is infeasible to enumerate injection forms across visual, voice, and covert-audio channels. Payloads transformed through font deformation, QR encoding, reverberation masking, cloned speech, or frequency modulation may bypass detectors. Television broadcasts, public signs, legitimate ultrasonic equipment, and authorized far-field speech may also produce false positives. Speaker verification and source localization degrade under noise, occlusion, and multi-speaker conditions, while real-time multimodal analysis adds inference latency and compute overhead.
